newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Extracts from European security summit documents.
newsitem.headline: Extracts from European security summit documents.

text.p: Following are extracts from the main declarations issued by a European security summit which ended on Tuesday, covering issues from Bosnia to arms control.
The texts were agreed by leaders from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
As we approach the new century, it is more important than ever that we build together a peaceful...region where all our nations and individuals feel secure.
We recognise that serious risks and challenges, such as those to our security and sovereignty, continue to be of major concern. We are committed to address them.
Respect for human rights remains fundamental to our concept of democracy... We are determined to consolidate the democratic gains of the changes that have occurred since 1989...

The OSCE will continue to play an important role in the promotion and consolidation of peace in Bosnia...We confirm that we will supervise the preparation and conduct of elections for the municipal governing authorities in 1997...
We welcome the OSCE's continuing focus on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
DECLARATION ON SECURITY MODEL FOR THE 21ST CENTURY

We are determined to learn from the tragedies of the past and to translate our vision of a cooperative future into reality by creating a common security space free of dividing lines in which all states are equal partners.

Our approach is one of cooperative security based on democracy, respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms and the rule of law, market economy and social justice. It excludes any quest for domination. It implies mutual confidence and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

We jointly commit ourselves...not to support participating states that threaten or use force in violation of international law against the territorial integrity or political independence of any participating state...(and) to attach importance to security concerns of all participating states irrespective of whether they belong to military structures or arrangements.

We reaffirm the inherent right of each and every participating state to be free to choose or change its security arrangements, including treaties of alliance, as they evolve. Each participating state will respect the rights of all others in this regard. They will not strengthen their security at the expense of the security of other states. Within the OSCE, no state, organisation or grouping can have any superior responsibility for maintaining peace and stability in the OSCE region, or regard any part of the OSCE region as its sphere of influence.

The further strengthening of stability through conventional arms control will be decisive for future European security. We welcome the decision of the CFE (1990 arms accord) states parties to adapt it to a changing security environment in Europe...
...We will consider developing a Charter on European Security which can serve the needs of our peoples in the new century.
